subject: Renewal: proposed consolidated flex-path + auto-renew opt-in (Nimbus Health)
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Leila Gomez <leila@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Nimbus Health Procurement <procurement@nimbushealth.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal: proposed consolidated flex-path + auto-renew opt-in (Nimbus Health)

Hi Leila —

Thanks again for the time last week. Attached is a concise renewal proposal that aims to simplify your footprint across our platform while giving Nimbus the runway to scale predictably:

Key points (summary):
- Term: 36 months (3-year) with graduated commit ramp: 40% year 1 / 70% year 2 / 100% year 3.
- Co-terming: We consolidate the three product SKUs onto a single co-terminus contract to simplify billing and reporting.
- Auto-renew opt-in: Renewal will auto-renew on anniversary with a 30-day opt-out window; customer must notify to opt-out.
- Burst/on-demand: Reserved commit covers baseline; we include a 20% burst window at discounted overage rates.
- Onboarding & migration credit: $50k onboarding credit in year 1 (applies to Redwood Console onboarding + dedicated capacity tuning).
- SLAs & credits: Standard SLA with a 0.5% credit kicker if monthly p95 latency exceeds agreed threshold for two consecutive months.

Attachments: Term_Proposal_Nimbus_20261109.pdf (proposal) and a short Mutual Action Plan spreadsheet with milestones and acceptance criteria.

Ask: Please review the term structure and the ramp percentages and confirm any internal constraints on billing cadence (monthly vs quarterly vs annual). If this aligns with Procurement's expectations I'll loop legal and pull a DocuSign-ready redline.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call to walk through the ramp math.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachment: Term_Proposal_Nimbus_20261109.pdf (PDF, 12 pages)
Attachment: Mutual_Action_Plan_NIM-2026-082.xlsx (Excel, 2 sheets)

From: Leila Gomez <leila@nimbushealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal: proposed consolidated flex-path + auto-renew opt-in (Nimbus Health)

Marcus —

Appreciate the clear summary and the MAP. A few quick clarifying questions from Procurement and Finance:

1) Billing cadence — Finance prefers quarterly billing if possible. Is the pricing model compatible with quarterly invoicing while keeping the commit/discount logic intact?
2) Ramp protection — can we add a true-up clause at the 12-month and 24-month marks instead of automatic annual true-up? Nimbus wants predictable spend windows.
3) Auto-renew opt-in — Procurement is wary of auto-renew without explicit pre-renew notice. Can we move to auto-renew with a 60-day notification (instead of 30)?

I'll need the proposal to show quarterly billing lines for internal approval. Also copying Procurement (procurement@nimbushealth.com) to coordinate legal.

Thanks,
Leila
Head of Procurement, Nimbus Health
leila@nimbushealth.com
+1 (617) 555-0124

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Leila Gomez <leila@nimbushealth.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 12:22:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Renewal: proposed consolidated flex-path + auto-renew opt-in (Nimbus Health)

Marissa / Karthik —

Looping you in: Nimbus asked for (a) quarterly billing, (b) true-up at month 12 & 24 vs automatic annual true-up, and (c) extend auto-renew notice from 30 -> 60 days.

Context: Their usage profile shows a steep onramp in Y2 (clinics onboarding), but Finance needs predictable quarterly cadence. They are sensitive to long auto-renew windows.

Questions:
- Karthik: can we keep the headline economics with quarterly billing? If so, what's the margin impact and any necessary contract language?
- Marissa: do we want to entertain 60-day notice for auto-renew or push back to 30? Any commercial levers we should offer to offset the increased risk (e.g., smaller onboarding credit or slightly reduced year-1 discount)?

Thanks — happy to discuss quickly.

—Marcus

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal: proposed consolidated flex-path + auto-renew opt-in (Nimbus Health)

Marcus / Marissa —

Quick math: quarterly billing is fine operationally — we can amortize the commit across quarters. Pricing impact is neutral if we keep the same annual effective commitment; however, two items to flag:

1) True-up cadence change (explicit true-ups at month 12 and 24) adds more administrative touchpoints and slightly increases collection risk; recommend we keep a modest overage buffer: change burst window from 20% to 15% and add an explicit 10% grace true-up cap in year 1 to avoid sticker-shock.

2) Auto-renew notice to 60 days — acceptable commercially, but we should require that the customer confirm intent by a simple signed notice or purchase order to re-enable any onboarding credits for the renewed term. This protects us from clients who auto-renew then immediately opt-out of commitments.

If Marissa is okay, we can present a revised proposal with: quarterly billing lines, true-ups at 12/24, burst 15%, year-1 grace true-up 10%, auto-renew 60-day notice with a condition on onboarding credit eligibility.

—Karthik
Head of Pricing Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Leila Gomez <leila@nimbushealth.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 09:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal: proposed consolidated flex-path + auto-renew opt-in (Nimbus Health)

Leila / Marcus / Karthik —

Thanks for the back-and-forth. I support Karthik's approach with the following slight edits to keep upsell motion healthy:
- Keep onboarding credit at $50k but vest it over the first two quarters (50% at go-live, 50% at quarter 2 milestone).
- Maintain a marketing/reference ask (one case study + logo use) in exchange for preserving the year-1 pricing band.
- Add a 90-day ramp protection clause wording that allows a single-cure true-up inside the first 90 days for unanticipated spikes (doesn't count toward the 12/24 true-up triggers).

If Nimbus agrees to the above, we will deliver a DocuSign-ready redline and pricing schedule showing quarterly billing. Marcus — please update the MAP with the vesting schedule and reference/case study milestone.

—Marissa
VP, Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Leila Gomez <leila@nimbushealth.com>, Nimbus Health Procurement <procurement@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal: proposed consolidated flex-path + auto-renew opt-in (Nimbus Health)

Leila —

Appreciate the quick review. Per your asks we've updated the proposal:
- Quarterly billing lines included in the attached pricing schedule.
- True-ups at month 12 and 24 (with a year-1 10% grace cap and a 90-day single-cure clause for unexpected early spikes).
- Auto-renew extended to 60-day notice; onboarding credit vesting schedule (50/50 over first two quarters) added.
- Marketing/reference clause included as discussed.

I've attached the revised Term_Proposal_Nimbus_20261113.pdf and updated MAP. If Procurement confirms this is acceptable I'll open the DocuSign envelope and route to legal for a final review.

Next step: Procurement confirmation on quarterly billing and legal redline. Happy to coordinate a short handoff call if helpful.

Best —
Marcus
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai
